newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil portworkers see little chance of strike now.
newsitem.headline: Brazil portworkers see little chance of strike now.

text.p: Brazilian portworkers have all but called off a national strike on Aug 11 after colleagues at three ports received collective wage offers, said Jose Peres Cesar, president of the National Portworkers' Federation. "There will no longer be a national strike," Cesar told Reuters.
The ports of Vitoria, Rio de Janeiro, Aratu and Salvador had received offers for a three percent salary raise, and all except for Vitoria had already signed new collective wage agreements, he said.

Administrative portworkers had threatened to call a national strike on Aug 11 unless Transport Minister Eliseu Padilha awarded them a collective wage rise of 15.52 percent. The last round of collective agreements expired on June 30. But they were now willing to settle for three percent, providing this included a provision to continue negotiating a more substantial increase, Cesar said.

The original July 31 deadline for Padilha to reply had been lifted and that no fresh deadline existed, he added. "In a meeting in Rio last week, we estimated that there could be some kind of a reply within the next few days," he said.
There was still a chance that some sort of partial strike would be held next week, although this was now sharply lower than a few weeks ago, Cesar said.
